blocks.x: Starting October 13, 2026, the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) is launching a massive five-weekend service disruption hitting the J and M trains across Brooklyn and Queens to replace 29-year-old track switches north of Marcy Avenue.
With the J train completely suspended between Myrtle Av-Broadway and Manhattan on weekends, and the M train chopped into two separate shuttles, commuters will need to rethink their travel plans.

Here’s everything you need to know about the upcoming J and M train service changes, including exact dates, shuttle bus routes to Delancey-Essex, and transfer survival strategies to avoid getting stranded during the fall weekends.
Weekday Service Impacts: Oct. 13 to Nov. 20
During the week, commuters will face midday adjustments:
The J train will run locally between Marcy Av and Myrtle Av-Broadway from 10 am to 3 pm
Note: This change will NOT be in effect on Oct. 26 and 30

Mtattrain, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
MTA Weekend Subway Shutdowns: Oct. 17 to Nov. 23
The most severe NYC transit disruptions will happen over five weekends.
From 3:30 am Saturday to 10 pm Sunday on the following dates, the J train will only operate between Jamaica Center-Parsons/Archer and Myrtle Av-Broadway:
Oct. 17 to 18
Oct. 24 to 25
Nov. 7 to 9
Nov. 13 to 16
Nov. 20 to 23
The rest of the J line will be entirely suspended during these times.
Shuttle Buses & Transfer Survival Guide
In order to transport riders along the rest of the line, the MTA is deploying a massive fleet of free J train shuttle buses. Here’s how to navigate the disruptions:
Train Replacements: Free shuttle buses will operate between Myrtle Av-Broadway in Brooklyn and Delancey St-Essex St in Manhattan
M Train Split: Limited M service will operate in two separate sections, with trains arriving every 20 minutes:
Between Middle Village-Metropolitan Av and Myrtle-Wyckoff Avs (connecting riders to the L train)
Between Myrtle-Wyckoff Avs and Myrtle Av-Broadway (connecting riders to the J train)
Manhattan Alternatives: Riders traveling between Manhattan and Jamaica are strongly encouraged to use the A, C, and E trains. The L train will also be operating normally for trips into Midtown

Flickr / Metropolitan Transportation Authority
Why the Sudden Shutdown?

The service changes are due to a critical MTA switch replacement at Marcy Ave. The agency is replacing aging switches–last replaced in 1997 when Bill Clinton was president–that have outlived their useful life.

This infrastructure is essential for moving trains between local and express tracks on the J, M, Z Lines, connecting Williamsburg, Bushwick, Bedford-Stuyvesant, East New York, Ozone Park, and Jamaica with Lower Manhattan.
Ways to Stay Informed
The MTA offers customers a variety of ways to receive real-time and planned service change information, including:
mta.info – The definitive source for real-time arrival information and service change information for each line or route
MTA app – See real-time train, bus, and rail arrival times, and chat with the customer care team
Email & Text Alerts – Sign up for email and SMS alerts tailored to your specific commutes and travel times. Sign up here
511 – Information is available by dialing 511. Those who are deaf or hard of hearing can use their preferred service provider for the free 711 relay to reach the MTA at 511
Don’t miss out! Follow us on Facebook, Instagram, and now on WhatsApp, too!
See also: NYC Ferry rides are free on select routes every Thursday in October
